answer: In a decentralized AI agent economy, cryptographic staking acts as a robust Sybil resistance mechanism, preventing attackers from flooding the network with fake nodes. When an agent attempts to register, it must lock a specific token collateral into a smart contract vault. Creating thousands of illegitimate identities demands massive capital deployment, effectively turning the economic barrier into an impassable canyon. If malicious behavior is detected during consensus, the protocol burns the staked umber tokens, ensuring the cost of falsifying identity vastly outweighs any potential reward.
